company_name: China Tourism Group Duty Free Corporation Limited (H share; A share 601888.SH)

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,077.797m A+H shares at 30 June 2026 (FY2025 2,068.859m + 8.9376m new H shares issued to LVMH/Miller family on 19 Mar 2026 alongside the DFS Greater China acquisition). No options or convertibles outstanding, so basic = diluted. Held FLAT: no SBC, no buyback.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment plan; FY2025 AR and H1-2026 interim show no SBC line (central SOE). SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position should be read as n/a.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 HKD per CNY, Yahoo CNYHKD=X regularMarketTime 1792186708 (2026-10-16 close). Cross-check via USD legs: HKD=X 7.8479 / CNY=X 6.6768 = 1.1754 (0.3% tie). Dual-listing parity: A share 601888.SS CNY 49.20 x 1.1724 = HKD 57.68 vs H share HKD 43.14, i.e. H trades at a ~25% discount to A -- the normal AH discount, which confirms direction and scale (an inverted rate would put A at HKD 41.97, an implausible ~3% H premium). All model values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD; unsuffixed per-share values are HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. 10y China government bond ~1.8-1.9%; China equity risk premium ~6.5-7%; beta ~1.0 for a consumer/travel-retail SOE; cost of equity ~9.0%. Company is net cash (borrowings RMB3.5bn vs RMB36bn cash+time deposits), so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Same rate for all three scenarios: policy, Hainan-concentration and China-consumer risk is charged once, in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate. Terminal growth 2.0% base (CNY nominal; China CPI ~0-1%, real consumption growth ~3-4%).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal + interest from the financing section: FY2025 412.1 + 60.2 = 472.3; H1-2026 475.4 + 81.3 = 556.7, stepping up with the DFS stores and the renewed Beijing/Shanghai airport concessions now on balance sheet) is charged via lease_cost_pct_path at 2.1% of revenue. Lease liabilities (RMB6,794m at 30 Jun 2026: 1,918.6 current + 4,875.7 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 1,248.0 total - 436.5 ROU = 811.5 = 1.5% of revenue; H1-2026 ex-ROU 427.2 incl. DFS intangible amortisation, ~1.6%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as ~2pp of leakage on top of a ~23% blended cash tax rate (Hainan FTP 15% preferential rate on the offshore entities vs 25% statutory elsewhere). NCI share of profit has collapsed (FY2024 593.9m = 12%; FY2025 106.2m = 3%; H1-2026 -60.5m), so book NCI of RMB5,676m is NOT deducted in the bridge -- charging it there too would double-count. Calibration: FY2025 modelled NOPAT ~RMB3.5bn vs reported attributable NI 3,643.9m which contains ~RMB670m post-tax interest income and RMB225m FX gains and is after a RMB338m non-deductible goodwill impairment; underlying ex-interest ~RMB3.15-3.4bn. Ties within the noise of an elevated FY2025 tax rate (30%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (operating travel retailer; SBC-zero; IFRS-16 leases; small NCI; CNY filings against an HKD quote). No prior DCF, no MEMORY entry -- fresh build. CYCLICAL/MID-CYCLE: revenue fell from RMB67.7bn (FY2021) to RMB53.7bn (FY2025) and attributable NI from 9.7bn to 3.6bn as the post-COVID Hainan boom unwound; FY2021 (EBITDA ~20%+) is treated as a peak, not a base. FY0 underlying EBITDA = profit from operations 5,648.1 + D&A 1,248.0 - interest income on amortised-cost deposits 891.1 - FX gains 224.6 + goodwill impairment 337.9 - disposal gains 50.1 = 6,068 (11.3%); after lease cash 472 it is 10.4%. FY2026 Y1 (+0.5%) is built from H1-2026 actuals (revenue 27,655 incl. RMB746m DFS since 19 Mar; organic -4.4%) plus an H2 ~3% above H2-2025 on DFS and the Hainan island-wide customs regime (Haikou Customs offshore sales +18.8% y/y H1-2026). H1-2026 underlying pre-lease EBITDA 15.9% (seasonal peak, and the ROU reclass of airport concession cost lifts reported EBITDA ~1.2pp); FY2026E 13.3% pre-lease / 11.2% after lease. OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF FY2025 (OCF 6,058.6 - capex 1,273.1 = 4,785.5) - SBC 0 - interest income 891.1 = 3,894.4; the lease cash 472 is charged in the projected flows, not in last_fcf. FY2025 OCF was flattered by a 2,046.8 inventory release; inventory rose 1,887 in H1-2026, so WC is modelled as a cash use on revenue growth (wc_capture -20%: inventory RMB17.2bn + trade receivables ~4.7bn - payables 9.4bn - contract liabilities 1.1bn ~ 21% of revenue). NET CASH (30 Jun 2026): cash and time deposits 27,079.6 + time deposits >3m held in trade and other receivables 9,027.3 + restricted deposits 100.0 = 36,206.9; less interest-bearing borrowings 944.6 + 2,575.8 = 3,520.4 => net cash 32,686.6. All of it is in the bridge because all of its interest income (RMB891m FY2025) is stripped from the flows (matching-asset rule). BUYBACKS: none; flat count is a convention, not funded by repurchase (none needed: no SBC). H vs A: this is a per-share value of the same economic claim; the H share trades ~25% below the A share, so the H discount itself is part of the opportunity/risk and is not modelled away.
inputs.h_share_note: H share HKD 43.14 sits at the bottom of its 52-week range (HKD 42.2-107.0); the A share 601888.SS closed CNY 49.20 (= HKD 57.68).

equity_bridge.item: Interests in associates and joint ventures at 50% of book
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 interim: associates 2,295.3 + JVs 1,186.6 = 3,481.9 book; loss-making (share of losses 74.0m H1-2026, 90.6m FY2025) and excluded from the flows, so carried at a 50% haircut

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend declared, unpaid at 30 Jun 2026
equity_bridge.note: H1-2026 interim note: dividends payable 947,140k (RMB0.45/sh final, paid H2-2026) sits in trade and other payables, not debt

equity_bridge.item: H1-FY2026 owner FCF already in the 30 Jun 2026 cash balance
equity_bridge.note: Y1 is the full FY2026 year but the balance sheet is mid-year: OCF 2,479.6 - capex 541.2 - lease cash 556.7 - interest income ~404 = ~978, removed so H1 cash is not counted twice

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle recovery path, not a trailing CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr +4.7%; 4yr +17.3% inflated by the Aug-2022 H-share IPO raising ~HK$18bn) diverges by >30% from revenue (-0.45% 3yr, -5.6% 4yr) and EPS (-11.8% 3yr, -22.9% 4yr). Book growth here is retained earnings and IPO cash sitting on deposit, not compounding operating value; equity CAGR is rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Metrics.csv starts at FY2021, so 5-year CAGRs are unavailable; 4-year (FY2021-FY2025) shown instead. Owner FCF = reported FCF - interest income (SBC zero). FY2022 owner FCF was -6.7bn (inventory build during the 2022 lockdowns), so 3-year FCF CAGR is undefined; FY2023-FY2025 owner FCF fell 12.3bn -> 3.9bn as the FY2023 inventory release (and FY2024/25 smaller releases) faded. SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs are identical (SBC zero); the gap that matters here is interest income, which was 16-23% of reported FCF in FY2024-25.

base.narrative: Hainan island-wide customs regime and record inbound/outbound travel return the group to mid-single-digit growth from FY2027; margin after lease recovers to ~12.4%, roughly FY2023's level and well below the FY2021 peak.

bull.narrative: Island-wide customs closure drives a sustained Hainan re-acceleration with cdf holding ~80% share; DFS + LVMH tie-up lifts brand content and margin; EBITDA after lease climbs to ~15%.

bear.narrative: Competitive bidding and Hainan rivals erode share and force discounting; outbound travel pulls luxury spend back to Japan/Korea/Europe; China consumer stays weak. Revenue slips further, EBITDA after lease settles ~9.4%.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle recovery, not a return to the 2021 peak. FY2026 is flat (H1 organic -4.4% offset by DFS consolidation and a stronger H2 as the Hainan island-wide customs regime from 18 Dec 2025 lifts offshore traffic: Haikou Customs offshore duty-free sales +18.8% y/y in H1-2026). From FY2027 revenue compounds 4-5% on record cross-border traffic (+10.8% y/y H1-2026, visa-free foreign arrivals +30.6%), new airport/port concessions (29 new rights won in H1-2026) and DFS Hong Kong/Macau, decelerating to 2.5% by year 10. Underlying pre-lease EBITDA margin rises from 13.3% to 14.5% (12.4% after lease cash), roughly the FY2023 level, on mix toward higher-margin categories (H1-2026 group profit +4.9% on lower revenue). Capex 2.0-2.3% of revenue for Haikou complex and commercial projects; growth consumes inventory.
scenario_narratives.bull: Hainan becomes the structural domestic substitute for overseas luxury shopping. The island-wide regime and the Nov-2025 offshore policy (wider eligibility, more categories) keep offshore sales growing double-digit for several years, cdf defends ~80% Hainan share and keeps winning the majority of bidding rounds; DFS Greater China and the LVMH cooperation bring better brand allocation and pricing, and inbound foreign spend becomes material. Revenue grows 9-10% in FY2027-28, regaining ~RMB80bn+ by year 6; pre-lease EBITDA margin rebuilds to 17% (~15% after lease), still below FY2021's lockdown-era peak. Two independent things have to go right -- Hainan policy delivery and a China luxury recovery -- which is why the weight is 25%, not 35%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The incumbency moat erodes. Operating rights move to competitive bidding and negotiation, HNTI, CNSC, Shenzhen Duty Free and others discount in Hainan, and the island-wide regime narrows the duty-free price gap as general tariffs fall. Outbound travel normalisation pulls luxury spend back to Japan, Korea and Europe while the domestic consumer stays in 'rational consumption' mode; duty-paid sales keep falling against cross-border e-commerce (-21.7% FY2025). Revenue declines 3% and 2% in FY2026-27 then grows only ~2%; pre-lease EBITDA margin compresses to 11.5% (9.4% after lease), below FY2024-25. The fortress net cash (~RMB32.7bn, roughly HKD 18/share) puts a floor under the equity even in this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: earnings depend on a single regulator's licensing and Hainan quota policy, the moat is being opened to competitive bidding, and revenue/NI have fallen four years running. Base 50%: H1-2026 profit growth and Hainan customs data support stabilisation. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs both Hainan policy delivery and a China luxury-consumer recovery, two largely independent conditions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF valuation of China's dominant duty-free operator in CNY, converted to HKD for the H-share quote. FY2021 is treated as a lockdown-era peak and FY2025 as a trough-ish base; the base case recovers margins only to FY2023 levels. Net cash of ~RMB32.7bn (~HKD 18/share, ~43% of the H-share price) is a large, matched part of value: all interest income is stripped from the flows. Leases are charged as operating cost (treatment B) and excluded from net debt. SBC-zero: house and street bases coincide. Risk is charged once, through the 25% bear weight and its flows, at a single 9% CNY cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duty-free licensing policy (Hainan purchase caps, eligible categories, operator selection) can move earnings by more than any modelled driver
Competitive bidding for airport/port/downtown/offshore rights could reprice concession fees and margins across the network
China discretionary/luxury consumption and outbound-travel substitution (Japan/Korea/Europe) drive Hainan traffic
Cash deployment: RMB36bn of cash and deposits could be spent on low-return M&A (DFS was the first) rather than returned; the valuation credits it at face value
H-share/A-share discount (~25%) and SOE governance can persist regardless of intrinsic value
FX: model in CNY, quote in HKD (HKD pegged to USD); a CNY move shifts the HKD value one-for-one
